page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is a virtual machine configuration within the low-memory Dlsv6 family. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor using the x86_64 architecture, configured with 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Clock speeds reach up to 4.2 GHz, supplemented by 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is set to 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (2.0 GB per core). The instance includes hardware support for modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and VAES cryptography. It does not provision hardware GPU accelerators, includes no local storage, and assigns zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate distinct compute performance characteristics. Single-threaded efficiency is notably high, driven by the 4.2 GHz clock rate and instruction set optimizations, as demonstrated by strong results in Geekbench single-core testing (2115.0), single-threaded gzip compression (31.28 GB/sec), and text processing (2529.0). In contrast, total parallel compute capacity is constrained by the 4 vCPU topology, reflected in lower-tier stress-ng multi-core (3908.06) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression marks. Memory subsystem performance is also comparatively modest, with PassMark memory scoring in the bottom tier alongside large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measuring 36.43 GB/sec and 25.65 GB/sec respectively.

The 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio makes the D4ls_v6 a cost-efficient alternative to standard 1:4 general-purpose instances for tasks where memory overhead is unnecessary. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires remote storage attachments for persistence, and memory-intensive applications will face resource limitations. Workload fit is optimal for single-thread bound microservices, entry-level static web serving, build steps without heavy compilation overhead, and small-model CPU-based inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine optimized for lower-memory footprint computing. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores), 8.0 GB of system memory, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong single-core performance, achieving 2115.0 in Geekbench single-core and fast single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth benchmarks occupy average to lower tiers due to the 4 vCPU count and 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The D4ls_v6 is technically suited for CPU-focused workloads with modest RAM requirements, such as lightweight web servers, text processing pipelines, and small CPU-driven AI inference.
